Quick triage notes (what I can see from our edge telemetry):
- Around 07:40–07:50 PDT we see increased packet retransmits and tail latency for flows terminating in us-east-1 edge.
- Traces to Cobalt show asymmetric routing: their traceroute exits via partner-peering-3 while return traffic flows through a different NAT/proxy in our upstream (seen in flow logs).
- DNS lookups for their subdomain show elevated TTL misses and occasional timeouts (not many, but enough to exacerbate cache misses).
- Connection hangs appear upstream of our inference runtime (we’re seeing TCP handshake retransmits and a cluster of 502s from the edge reverse proxy).

Immediate recommendations:
1) Ask Cobalt to temporarily reduce resolved TTL to 30s (short term) — reduces stale route stickiness.
2) Flip traffic to our backup peering (edge-peering-b) for the affected prefix — low-risk, can be live in ~12–15 mins.
3) Throttle large batched jobs from Cobalt for 30 minutes to reduce pressure on NAT gateways.

I’ll open a GCP support case for the NAT gateway saturation and request an expedited routing check. Monica — can you push the peering failover and coordinate the runbook?

-Rishi

Subject: Re: GCP case GCP-CS-Case-987654321: NAT gateway & upstream proxy rate-limits

Hi team — GCP network ops here. Summary of findings so far:
- One regional NAT gateway exhibited ephemeral port regeneration delays under burst load — manifested as TCP handshake delays and 502s at the edge. We are increasing ephemeral port pool size for the affected gateway (ETA ~30 min).
- We also observed stateful proxy rate-limiting on the upstream vendor appliance (third-party) that was dropping repeated HTTP/TCP sessions coming from the peered path. We’ve requested the vendor lift the temporary limit for traffic originating from Cobalt’s ASN while we stabilize.
- DNS: authoritative looked healthy, but intermediate cache TTLs in the provider network were inconsistent for a short period — we recommend Cobalt lower TTLs briefly and we’ll add a short cache warm-up period after failover.

Temporary mitigations suggested:
- Continue traffic steering to edge-peering-b for 45–60 minutes while NAT pool is adjusted.
- Vendor to remove rate-limit; if not possible, we can set up temporary source-NAT at a different gateway.

We’ll update case GCP-CS-Case-987654321 with progress.

— GCP NetOps
